correctness.rationale: The hub deletion is exactly the full simplex for r >= maximum arm length. The invariant hub-link subcomplex omitting an interior vertex has an explicit fiberwise terminal-toggle acyclic matching and one critical vertex; the fully selected interior fiber has precisely binomial(b-1,t) top critical cells in dimension r-2. The patchwork acyclicity argument works for all b>=3 and all arm lengths >=3. The link suspension produces the asserted integral sphere wedge. Relative integral chains are the truncated Koszul contraction complex on the endpoint permutation module with an orientation determinant on interior vertices; its highest kernel is wedge^t ker(sum), yielding the exact torsion-free integral automorphism module. The embedded standard-library checker passed 158 complete finite mod-two homology/acyclicity checks and 576 independent Lefschetz comparisons, but the proof does not rely on bounded experiments.

value.rationale: The stable-range classification solves a natural unexplored higher-independence invariant for arbitrarily heterogeneous long-arm spiders, with a sharp binomial sphere-count window depending only on b and aggregate interior count N rather than arm distribution. Its explicit integral automorphism module distinguishes odd/even subdivision parity, giving information unforced by ranks or vertex decomposability. Excluded b=2 paths and all-length-two spiders avoid routine-covered specializations. Both the exact binomial ranks and parity-twisted module address motivated structural topology questions and are reusable in equivariant homology calculations.
